h: Science, Rugby and a Spin on the Ice
p: Widnes has a couple of brilliant extras worth adding to your day. Catalyst Science Discovery Centre sits at Spike Island, right where the town's chemical industry was born, and it's packed with hands-on exhibits that kids love. There's a glass lift up to an observation gallery with great views over the Mersey and the bridges, too. It's a natural follow-up to an hour on the ice, especially if the weather isn't playing ball.
Sports fans will know Widnes as a proper rugby league town, home of the Widnes Vikings, so you might catch a match day buzz if you're visiting in season.

For the skating itself, it's all about getting the basics right. Choose comfortable layers, gloves and long socks. Get your hire skates laced tightly at the ankle so your foot feels supported. Start near the barrier, take small steps, and keep your knees bent. Falling is part of the fun, but tuck your hands in and get up quickly so nobody skates over your fingers.

Groups of mates and families often find the best part is the cheering. The first full lap without holding on is a big moment, so make sure somebody's ready with a phone to capture it. Just don't film while skating yourself. That never ends well.
